title: Dinosaurs: King, Rock, Birds
description: A name that means something fierce, a crash that ended an age, and a twist in your backyard—Go Deep into dino lore.

questions.question: Scientists named the biggest meat-eater 'Tyrannosaurus rex.' Broken into Greek and Latin, what does that name mean?
questions.explanation: 'Tyrannos' is Greek for tyrant, 'sauros' means lizard, and 'rex' is Latin for king—so the full name is basically 'king of the tyrant lizards.'

questions.question: That tyrant lizard king lived in which time period—the last age of the dinosaurs, after the Jurassic?
questions.hint: It starts with 'Cre-' and comes after the Jurassic
questions.explanation: T. rex lived near the very end of the Cretaceous. Wild fact: it lived closer in time to you than to Stegosaurus!

questions.question: The Cretaceous ended 66 million years ago when what kind of space rock crashed into Earth?
questions.explanation: The rock was about 6 miles wide—roughly the width of a big city. It hit so hard it changed the climate of the whole planet.

questions.question: That asteroid left a giant buried crater near which Mexican peninsula—home of Cancún?
questions.explanation: The Chicxulub crater is more than 100 miles across and lies partly under the sea off the Yucatán. You can stand on the rim and not even know it's there.

questions.question: After the Yucatán impact, one group of dinosaurs survived and still lives today—look up, or at a chicken. What are they?
questions.hint: Look up at the sky—or at a chicken!
questions.explanation: Birds are living dinosaurs. The pigeon on your sidewalk is a distant cousin of T. rex—and that king lived closer in time to you than to Stegosaurus.

easterEgg.title: Closer to us than Stegosaurus
easterEgg.text: T. rex lived at the very end of the dinosaur age. Stegosaurus had already been extinct for about 80 million years. So T. rex is closer in time to you than to Stegosaurus.
